paper_metadata.title: Quantum Arithmetic for Directly Embedded Arrays

summary: This paper proposes a theoretical gate-based framework for direct embedding of arrays into quantum amplitudes, with a two-register quantum matrix and an auxiliary qubit for loading/readout. It reports asymptotic costs such as O(2^n) CNOTs for generic n-qubit state preparation, nI x-gates plus 2 y-rotations and 1 multi-controlled NOT for constant-array loading, and a classical baseline of J operations for loading a constant array on a line of the matrix, but it does not demonstrate a practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Theoretical gate-based framework for direct embedding of arrays into quantum amplitudes, with implemented and tested arithmetic operations in Qiskit; includes example manipulations such as constant shift and approximate linear shift of an oracle.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-register quantum matrix |psi> = sum_{i,j} c_ij |i>_nI |j>_nJ with direct embedding of values into amplitudes; auxiliary qubit used for loading and readout. Example operations act on rows/columns via masking and controlled rotations/CNOTs.

problem_instance.description: Generic I x J arrays / matrices and example oracles; no specific benchmark dataset. Example 5.1 shifts a loaded oracle by a constant; Example 5.2 approximates a linear shift with step functions.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uniform distribution loaded first; then pointwise or constant-array loading into amplitudes using masking and controlled Ry rotations. Example 5.2 uses piecewise-constant step approximation to a linear shift.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Implemented and tested using Qiskit; no numerical benchmark protocol, shot counts, or statistical evaluation procedure reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Direct embedding/loading requires normalization by infinity norm; masking/unmasking of row/column registers; controlled Ry rotations for loading values; Hadamard-based sum/reduction; Grover-style amplification described for readout.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Quantum Coin / amplitude estimation style readout with iterative Grover amplification; empirical confidence interval and repeated measurements used conceptually.

classical_baselines.method_name: classical memory copy for constant array loading

speedup_claims.factor: exponentially fewer operations for loading a constant array
speedup_claims.conditions: for loading a constant array; quantum loading cost depends on number of rows controlled
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this is more interesting from a quantum speed-up perspective than pointwise loading, but does not provide a formal end-to-end speedup proof.

speedup_claims.factor: O(2^n) CNOTs for generic n-qubit state preparation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: state preparation by classical/standard loading methods
speedup_claims.conditions: generic real array loading; current state of the art via multiplexors or Schmidt decomposition
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity statement, not an empirical benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: State preparation for a generic n-qubit state scales as O(2^n) CNOTs; constant-array loading uses nI x-gates, two y-rotations, and one multi-controlled NOT in worst case; arithmetic operations depend on masking/control overhead.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Loading a constant array on a line of the I x J matrix requires J operations; generic pointwise loading is classical O(IJ) in the obvious sense.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No concrete hardware execution, qubit count, or benchmarked runtime is reported; the paper is a theoretical framework with Qiskit implementation/testing only.
limiting_factors: No experimental comparison against a classical implementation for the full framework
State preparation for generic arrays scales as O(2^n) CNOTs
Loading a generic real array is explicitly described as not efficient
Readout relies on iterative Grover amplification and repeated measurements
The paper does not report a concrete end-to-end speedup

notes: No specific hardware device is named; only Qiskit implementation/testing is reported, so hardware.type is left not_specified.
